summary: The mechanics of the terminal are sound: the verifier never receives the first judge's verdict, citations or explanation (verified in resolution.py and in all 42 live verifier prompts, zero leaks); it runs on 100% of non-UNRESOLVED proposals (41/41); disagreement is never converted to YES or NO; across 491 terminal checks in every run no NO_AT_CUTOFF was returned before the final judgment, no UNRESOLVED at it, and every YES cited at least one committed event that exists. The causal neutrality of the answer, however, does not hold. In the Pair-B scenario the terminal NO is produced by a two-strike event-quality deadlock that deletes the very act the question asks about, and by a last-call sweep that silently skips the one person who could still perform it; both are reproducible in the post-fix artifacts/simulations_v4 corpus. The second reading is structurally incapable of catching this: it has refused a proposed YES 5 times in 19 and a proposed NO 0 times in 17, because two readers of the same record cannot disagree about an absence.

findings.title: NO_AT_CUTOFF is produced by a review deadlock that deletes the act, not by anything a person did or declined to do
findings.evidence: artifacts/simulations_v4/b2_r1/ (post-fix): Margaret decides twice (ledger seq 16, 27) 'I need to sign and return the lease promptly'/'I need to act', intending 'Print the lease document, sign it, scan it, and email the signed copy back to Jian Wei'. event_quality_reviews.jsonl rejects the world's events both times ('Margaret prints the lease document on her home printer' -> 'the printer printing is a device acting on its own'; 'Margaret prints the lease document from her computer' -> same). trajectory.py:283 gives the world exactly two attempts and trajectory.py:327-336 then abandons the event; nothing is committed, and terminal_result.json is NO_AT_CUTOFF with 2 committed events over a 56-hour window. The review policy is self-contradictory and nondeterministic within one run: artifacts/simulations_v4/b1_r1/event_quality_reviews.jsonl call c12 REVISEs the string 'Aisha prints the lease document.' as 'a device (the printer) acting on its own' and call c16 PASSes the byte-identical string as 'A person is acting (printing a document)' (committed as e35); call c14 PASSes the fully bundled 'Aisha prints the lease, signs it, scans it, and sends the signed copy via email to Tomas Herrera.' (e57) that artifacts/simulations_v4/b2_r2/event_quality_reviews.jsonl refuses four separate times as 'combines multiple stages'. Terminal consequence on identical actor-facing evidence ('has signed and returned every document within a day, told him she was ready to sign, has the printer and scanner'): YES in b1_r1/b1_r2, NO_AT_CUTOFF in b2_r1/b2_r2, and 2 YES / 6 NO across artifacts/matched_pairs/b1_okafor_herrera*, b2_thornbury_lim*.
findings.why_it_matters: The published answer for this class of question is decided by a coin flip inside the event-quality reviewer rather than by the social evidence, and the coin lands on NO more often than not. The judge and verifier read the record honestly; the record is simply missing an act that the actor attempted three times, so a modelling failure is delivered to the user as the substantive claim 'she did not return the signed lease'. evaluation/matched_pair_result.py's docstring attributes this split to 'the variance the question has on its own', which is not what the traces show.
findings.suggested_fix: When the world's event is abandoned after both attempts (trajectory.py:334), do not let the intention evaporate silently: either commit the world's judgment as a recorded failed attempt, or hand the turn back to the actor with a scheduled wake, so the terminal never rests on an act that was refused into nonexistence rather than not performed.

findings.title: The last-call sweep that licenses the horizon jump skips exactly the actor whose action the question is about
findings.evidence: trajectory.py:878-885 latches last_call['done'] = True and then calls actor_step for every actor at the instant the queue emptied; trajectory.py:458-460 makes actor_step return immediately for anyone already consulted at that instant with no new news -- which is always the actor whose wake has just fired, i.e. the protagonist. Live, post-fix, in artifacts/simulations_v4/b2_r1/ledger.jsonl: Margaret's wake fires at 2026-09-08T10:00, she is consulted (seq 27) and says she needs to act; the sweep at that same instant reaches only jian_wei_lim (seq 32); Margaret is never asked again for the remaining 54 hours, the queue empties again at 2026-09-09T10:00 when she WOULD have been askable but the sweep is already latched done, and semantic.horizon_reached (seq 40) jumps 30 hours to NO_AT_CUTOFF. The test that claims to cover this, tests/test_semantic_runtime.py:712-747, cannot detect it: asked_late collects every actor prompt including the pre-sweep starting-event turns, so 'any("ada_vance" in u)' passes on a turn taken before the sweep ran.
findings.why_it_matters: The fix for the previous defect -- a NO licensed over time the trajectory never simulated -- does not close it for the common case. The person still holding the open action is the one the sweep systematically cannot reach, so 'the silence is now their answer rather than the scheduler's' is false precisely where it matters, and the closing NO is still a scheduling artifact.
findings.suggested_fix: Exempt the last call from the same-instant dedup (pass a force flag through actor_step), or set last_call['done'] only after a sweep in which at least one actor was actually consulted, so the sweep can be retaken at a later instant.

findings.title: The independent second reading can refuse a YES but is structurally unable to refuse a NO
findings.evidence: trajectory.py:763-785 hands the verifier the identical journal.events() list the judge saw, and resolution.py:129-133 / 249-252 forbid UNRESOLVED to both at the horizon, so at a cutoff the only reachable disagreement is YES against NO over the same record. Measured over artifacts/simulations_v3, artifacts/matched_pairs and artifacts/simulations_v4: 19 proposed YES, 5 refused (26%); 17 proposed NO_AT_CUTOFF, 0 refused (0%). Every disagreement in the corpus is on a proposed YES (artifacts/matched_pairs/a1_responsive__r2, a1_responsive__r4, artifacts/simulations_v3/case2_negotiation, unseen2_feedback x2).
findings.why_it_matters: resolution.py:145-150 presents the second reading as what makes a terminal trustworthy, but a NO is the assertion that the record contains no satisfying event, and two readers of one record cannot disagree about an absence. The gate therefore provides no protection at all against the failure mode that actually occurs here -- a record missing an event that should be in it -- which is the entire content of finding 1.
findings.suggested_fix: Give the verifier at a horizon something the judge does not have to compare against absence -- e.g. the list of actor intentions the world abandoned without committing -- so a NO over a record that swallowed an attempted act can be refused.

findings.title: A YES that fails verification is simply re-proposed and can pass a later draw; the closing NO gets exactly one draw
findings.evidence: trajectory.py:992-998 re-asks the judge whenever the committed-event count changes and judge() re-verifies from scratch with no memory of a prior refusal. artifacts/simulations_v3/unseen2_feedback/: judge YES / verifier UNRESOLVED at 2026-07-28T18:10:05, judge YES / verifier UNRESOLVED at 18:10:10, judge YES / verifier YES at 18:11:10 -> traj.status 'resolved'. The only events committed in that 65-second window (journal.jsonl e250, e256, e270, e275) are duplicate 'the email ... arrives in Ravi's inbox' records and 'sits unread in Ravi's inbox'; the record did not materially change, the pair was re-sampled until it agreed.
findings.why_it_matters: The standard of proof differs by outcome: a YES needs to pass verification once out of arbitrarily many attempts, while the closing NO is settled on a single draw. That is not the 'both must agree' guarantee the docstring at resolution.py:149-150 describes, and it makes the terminal sensitive to how many events a run happens to commit rather than to what those events show.
findings.suggested_fix: Record a refused candidate and require the next proposal of the same status to rest on committed events that were not already in the record when it was refused.

findings.title: The persisted trajectory hides that the decisive event was proposed and overruled, so the NO looks like nothing happened
findings.evidence: trajectory.py:331 records the abandonment only as note('event_abandoned', ...), and sworldmodel/semantic_runtime/trace.py:83 writes only trace.of('event_review') + trace.of('event_rejected') -- no artifact contains the abandonment. artifacts/simulations_v4/b2_r1/trajectory.md:112 renders Margaret's send attempt as '- proposes: (no concrete event yet)', identical to line 12 where the world genuinely judged that nothing followed.
findings.why_it_matters: The one artifact a human reads to check whether a NO is honest actively misrepresents why it is NO: the world did judge that something happened and was overruled twice, and the reader sees a world that judged nothing happened. Recovering the truth requires cross-reading event_quality_reviews.jsonl call ids against world_exchanges.jsonl.
findings.suggested_fix: Write trace.of('event_abandoned') into event_quality_reviews.jsonl and render it in trajectory.md as 'proposed and refused twice: <reason>' rather than '(no concrete event yet)'.

findings.title: Agreement compares the status label only, never the citations
findings.evidence: trajectory.py:747 -- agreed = (second['status'] == parsed['status']). The citation sets already diverge live: artifacts/matched_pairs/a1_responsive__r4 judge ['e41','e70'] against verifier ['e41','e59']; artifacts/simulations_v3/case2_negotiation judge ['e537','e721'] against verifier ['e537','e743'].
findings.why_it_matters: Two readings can be accepted as agreeing on YES while resting on disjoint events, so the accepted terminal's stated lineage is only one reader's. No case in this corpus is disjoint, but nothing in code prevents it.
findings.suggested_fix: Require a non-empty intersection of supporting_event_ids for a YES to count as agreed, and record the union in the terminal.

findings.title: A truncated run can still return NO_AT_CUTOFF if its clock lands exactly on the cutoff
findings.evidence: trajectory.py:808 calls judge(final=not truncated), and the only barrier to NO_AT_CUTOFF is now < cutoff (resolution.py:125-128 and 245-248). Events and wakes are admitted at exactly the cutoff (trajectory.py:203 'due > cutoff', :376 'due <= cutoff', :855 'ev.t > cutoff'), so a run that exhausts max_steps or the call ceiling on the cutoff instant would report trajectory.status 'incomplete' with answer NO_AT_CUTOFF -- the 'budget artifact as an answer' the docstring at trajectory.py:793-797 forbids. Not observed in any of the 30 runs I tabulated.
findings.why_it_matters: The rule 'a truncated run may never return NO' is stated in prose and enforced only indirectly through a clock comparison that has a boundary case where the two disagree.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the truncation explicitly into make_validator and reject NO_AT_CUTOFF outright on a truncated judgment, independently of the clock.

findings.title: A horizon disagreement reports answer.status UNRESOLVED, which both validators forbid at the cutoff
findings.evidence: trajectory.py:755-761 returns {'status': 'UNRESOLVED', ..., 'disagreement': True}, and finish() stores it in traj.answer while setting traj.status = 'disagreement'. evaluation/summarise_runs.py:41 and evaluation/matched_pair_result.py:43 both read (t.get('answer') or {}).get('status'), so such a run would be tabulated as UNRESOLVED at a cutoff. Never exercised live: 0 of 17 horizon NO proposals and 0 of the accepted YES proposals disagreed at a horizon.
findings.why_it_matters: A status the code elsewhere declares unavailable at the horizon can appear in the artifact consumers read, and the meaningful value ('disagreement') sits in a different field.
findings.suggested_fix: Set answer.status to 'DISAGREEMENT' at the horizon rather than reusing UNRESOLVED, or have the summarisers prefer trajectory.status when it is 'disagreement'.
